**WEBSEARCH VERIFICATION**:
 - (1) `contains(x, element) -> boolean` confirmed at [trino.io/docs/current/functions/array.html](https://trino.io/docs/current/functions/array.html): 'Returns true if the array `x` contains the `element`.' Tests membership.
 - (2) `cardinality(x) -> bigint` confirmed: 'Returns the cardinality (size) of the array `x`.' Also accepts MAP.
 - (3) `array_distinct(x) -> array` confirmed: 'Remove duplicate values.' Preserves order.
 - (4) `array_intersect` / `array_union` / `array_except` all confirmed with `(x, y) -> array` signature; results deduped.
 - (5) `element_at(array(E), index) -> E` confirmed: 'returns NULL when accessing an index larger than array length'; negative indices count from the end; 1-based.
 - (6) Iceberg `write.target-file-size-bytes` default 512 MB (536870912 bytes) confirmed via search results (Iceberg docs + multiple corroborating blog posts).
 - (7) `target-file-size-bytes` Spark DataFrameWriter option (NO `write.` prefix) confirmed in r13 already (verified at iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/spark-configuration 'Write options' table).
 - (8) `iceberg.target-max-file-size` Trino catalog config confirmed at [trino.io/docs/current/connector/iceberg.html](https://trino.io/docs/current/connector/iceberg.html) — 'Target maximum size of written files; the actual size may be larger', default 1GB.
 - (9) Trino session-property convention (hyphens → underscores) confirmed: catalog `iceberg.target-max-file-size` → session `iceberg.target_max_file_size` (Trino doc example: `max-partitions-per-writer` → session `max_partitions_per_writer`).
 - (10) `iceberg.target_max_file_size` as a literal session property name with underscores is NOT listed as a distinct property in the Trino docs page — it's the session-property form of the hyphenated catalog config (Trino's universal convention). Both forms are valid for the same setting.
 - (11) `spark.sql.iceberg.write.target-file-size-bytes` as a Spark session config DOES NOT EXIST per any source — confirmed FABRICATED.
